23.text: The owner of the herd, or of the larger part of it, occupies this place

24.text: by right. The eldest of the brothers, or his son, has preference over the

25.text: others. Thus, sometimes a young boy may have preference over all his uncles.

26.text: In the camps of the poor people, of which I have spoken before, the one

27.text: who is richer or stronger than the others will have the front place. In tem-

28.text: porary camps, — for instance, in those formed in trading-places by casual

29.text: comers, — the front place belongs to the first comer. All the others take

30.text: places according to the order in which they come; so that the last comer

31.text: occupies the rear place. The occupant of the front house is considered as the

32.text: chief of the camp. He orders the change of camping-place and of pasture-

33.text: ground, and designates the days for bringing the herd to the camp, for
